site.author: Reed Sokolski
site.tagline: A podcast about cassettes. We are sorry but not.

props.text: Season 4 · 12 episodes · Tuesdays at 6:03 a.m. EST
A podcast about cassette tapes. The last format you remember holding.

Episode 47 is 38 minutes long. We promised 30. We are sorry but not. Each season we pick a physical format that almost made it and find the people who built their lives around it. Vinyl was season one. MiniDisc was season two. CompactFlash was season three, which a normal person would not consider a physical format, but we are not normal. Cassettes are season four. We have 11 more episodes after this one. We will probably stop after that. Probably.
What this is, with unnecessary precision.

Cassette is a podcast hosted by Reed Sokolski, a 41-year-old who works in inventory management at a regional grocery chain in Cleveland. He is not a journalist. He owns 312 cassette tapes, mostly inherited from his uncle Theo, who worked in radio between 1978 and 2009. Reed records every episode in his basement on a Shure SM7B he bought used in 2019 for $279. The audio quality is fine. It is not great.

Each episode follows a strict format because Reed gets uncomfortable with improvisation. There is a 4-minute cold open about a specific tape, a 22-minute interview with somebody who has a real relationship to the format (a duplication-plant supervisor, a Walkman engineer, the woman who runs the last tape store in Pittsburgh), and a 10-minute closing essay. Sometimes Reed runs over by 8 minutes. He blames it on the interview. He is usually lying.

There is no Patreon. There is one sponsor per episode. The sponsor is read for 47 seconds in the middle of the show. If you do not like that, you can fast forward, which is a feature cassettes did not have, and which we will discuss in episode 51.

props.quote: I listen to Cassette while I do my laundry on Tuesday mornings. The interview with Hannelore Brandt about chrome dioxide tape made me cry, which I did not see coming, but I am 53 and that is allowed.
props.author: Daria Knox

props.quote: Reed says 'we are not normal' once per episode and I have started waiting for it like a bird call. The show is more researched than it has any right to be. Episode 43 has 22 footnotes. I read all of them.
props.author: Marcus Hyde

props.quote: I am the woman who runs the last tape shop in Pittsburgh. Reed came in for episode 42 with a list of 31 questions. He asked 6 of them. The other 25 were better than mine would have been.
props.author: Sue Pasternak

props.quote: I work at the duplication plant in Springfield, Missouri. We make about 4,000 cassettes a week, mostly for indie labels. Cassette the podcast is the only piece of media that has ever gotten our work right. We listen on the line.
props.author: Vince Marrero

content.heading: Sponsor the show.
content.subheading: We do not work with brands we cannot use. We have turned down 9 sponsorships in the last year. We are bad at sales. You will get a fair read.

props.text: He reads everything. He answers most things, eventually, sometimes from his phone in the grocery store parking lot. Episode tips and corrections especially welcome.
